Package eu.cloudhopper.mc.runtime

Class Authenticator

java.lang.Object
eu.cloudhopper.mc.runtime.Authenticator
public final class Authenticator extends Object
Checks the caller's token on routes with @HttpTrigger(authenticated = true); the generated handlers call it before the function. Configuration properties of the deployment:
  • cloudhopper.auth.issuer (required): the issuer of the OpenID Connect provider, exactly as in the tokens' iss claim, e.g. https://cognito-idp.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/eu-central-1_AbC123
  • cloudhopper.auth.audience (required): the expected aud claim (for access tokens of Amazon Cognito: the client_id of the app client)
  • cloudhopper.auth.jwks-uri: the address of the provider's key set; without it, the jwks_uri of <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration
  • cloudhopper.auth.jwks: the key set itself as JSON (or Base64-encoded JSON), for providers the functions cannot reach; then nothing is fetched

No token: 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer; an invalid or expired token: 401; a valid token without a required scope: 403. The reason goes to the log, not to the client.

  • Method Details

    • authenticate

      public static Claims authenticate(Map<String,String> headers, String... scopes)
      Verifies the bearer token of a request.
      Parameters:
      headers - the request headers, keyed case-insensitively
      scopes - the scopes the token must have
      Returns:
      the claims of the token
      Throws:
      HttpStatusException - 401 without a valid token, 403 without a required scope
      IllegalStateException - if the issuer or audience is not configured, or the keys cannot be fetched
